newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Prodi sees Italy in EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees Italy in EMU in 1999.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he was convinced that Italy would be a founding member of Europe's single currency and that the country would meet the deficit and inflation criteria in 1998.
"The chances are more than 100 percent," Prodi told reporters after talks with Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima.
"We have started the preparations for the 1998 budget. We will meet even the strictest rules of the deficit and inflation criteria, except, of course, for the debt criteria," he said.

The European Union's Maastricht Treaty requires countries wanting to join European economic and monetary union to cut their budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product and their public debt to near 60 percent in 1997.

Italy's 1996 deficit ratio was 6.7 percent. It has pledged to reach this year the three percent goal laid down by the treaty and has introduced some 78 trillion lire of deficit cuts in the past five months to meet that target.
The European Commission has forecast Italy's 1997 deficit at 3.2 percent and the 1998 shortfall at 3.9 percent.
